research_question: In women undergoing surgery for stress or stress-predominant urinary incontinence, do single-incision mid-urethral slings (any device except TVT-Secur) achieve higher rates of subjective cure or improvement of incontinence at 12 months than transobturator mid-urethral slings (TOT/TVT-O)?
treatment_label: Single-incision mini-sling (SIS; e.g. Ajust, Needleless/Contasure, MiniArc, Ophira, Altis, Solyx — excluding TVT-Secur)
control_label: Transobturator mid-urethral sling (TOT/TVT-O, inside-out or outside-in)
outcome_description: Number of women reporting subjective (patient-reported) cure or improvement of stress urinary incontinence out of the number analysed in each arm at the 12-month follow-up. Patient-reported success is defined as the paper defines it (e.g. no stress leakage on questionnaire such as ICIQ-UI/UDI-6/ISI, 'very much better' or 'much better' on PGI-I/global impression of improvement, or satisfaction-based success). Objective cure measures (cough stress test, pad test, urodynamics) are not used. If a report covers longer follow-up (24 or 36 months), the 12-month figures are extracted from its tables/figures; if 12 months is unavailable, the closest earlier assessment of at least 6 months is used. Arms are assigned by device description, not column position, with SIS always the treatment arm. For trials with more than one eligible single-incision arm, each SIS arm is compared with the shared TOT group whose events and sample size are divided equally across comparisons; any TVT-Secur arm is ignored. Multiple reports of the same trial are extracted once, preferring the report giving the 12-month subjective result.
positive_direction: A positive effect (RR > 1) means a greater proportion of women were subjectively cured or improved with the single-incision sling than with the transobturator sling.
search_queries: single-incision mini-sling versus transobturator tape randomized trial stress urinary incontinence
MiniArc Ajust Solyx Altis Ophira Contasure needleless TVT-O comparison subjective cure
mid-urethral sling randomised controlled trial women stress incontinence 12 month cure rate
inclusion_criteria: Studies of adult women treated surgically for stress or stress-predominant urinary incontinence
Compares a single-incision mini-sling device (other than TVT-Secur alone) with a transobturator mid-urethral sling (TOT or TVT-O)
Reports some quantitative patient-reported cure/improvement or success data at a follow-up of roughly 6 months or more (event counts, proportions, or data from which they can be derived)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, narrative review, editorial, commentary, opinion or purely theoretical/protocol paper)

No comparison between a single-incision sling arm and a transobturator sling control arm (e.g. TVT-Secur only, or sling versus colposuspension, bulking agents or retropubic sling, or single-arm case series)
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no event counts/proportions, means+SDs, t/F values or odds ratios)
Completely unrelated to surgical treatment of female stress urinary incontinence
moderators_to_extract: Single-incision device type (MiniArc, Ajust, Solyx, Altis, Ophira, Contasure-Needleless, other)
Transobturator comparator route (inside-out TVT-O vs outside-in TOT)
Definition of subjective success (no leakage on questionnaire vs global impression vs satisfaction)
Follow-up timepoint actually used (12 months vs closest earlier ≥6 months)
Risk of bias / allocation concealment and blinding
effect_size_note: Pool as a risk ratio of subjective cure/improvement, SIS divided by TOT, using event counts and number analysed per arm; RR > 1 favours the single-incision sling. Random-effects pooling on the log RR scale.
single_outcome_target: subjective cure or improvement of stress urinary incontinence at 12 months
